body: @Mickeon I did read that comment previously. My opinion is whether you use a local RNG instance or the one in global scope shouldn't be based on how advanced the functions you want to use are. For example, if you're writing a single player game without seeded levels, you don't necessarily need reproducibility. If want to use rand_weighted functionality in this case you either are forced into creating a local RNG instance without needing to otherwise, or replicating the functionality. Considering that local and global scope RNG instances are the same object, I feel that the main difference between them should be that local instances are easier to keep track of when focusing on reproducibility. Of course this is just my opinion.

> Not being in the global scope is intentional. Weighted randomization is something you generally want more control over, and is more advanced than your typical "randomization" function.

@Mickeon I don't really get this reasoning. Nothing is stopping users from creating an instance of RandomNumberGenerator if they need to control the seed or state for rand_weighted (or any of the other rand functions), but if that's not needed then there's no downside to just using the global RNG instance. Most of the GDScript implementations of weighted randomness I see from users online only use the global rand functions, so it's clearly not a universal requirement. I see no reason why rand_weighted should be the only RandomNumberGenerator function not accessible in global scope.
